paper.title: Confucius Code Agent: Scalable Agent Scaffolding for Real-World Codebases
paper.central_claim: Scaffolding (orchestration, memory, tool abstractions) can matter as much as or more than the backbone; CCA, built on the Confucius SDK with a meta-agent and persistent notes, reaches 59% Resolve@1 on SWE-Bench-Pro exceeding prior research and commercial results under identical repositories, backbone and tool access.

gap.author_gap: Existing research-grade coding agents struggle on production-scale workloads and production systems lack extensibility; agent behaviour (prompts, tool wiring) is static and hand-designed; long-context (C1) and long-term memory (C2) challenges.
gap.checked_gap: Real but diffuse. Context overflow is evidenced inside the paper (trajectories exceed token limits without control); the claim that flat histories / heuristic prompts limit scale is not backed by a measured baseline failure analysis. The RSI-relevant fixed object is hand-designed prompts/tool wiring, changed by the meta-agent.

rs_pattern.reason: Opus sides with sol on identification, with low fit. The two parts scored as RSI are (a) a meta-agent that rewrites the hand-designed prompts, tool wrappers and error messages of a coding scaffold from test traces, and (b) persistent notes read back as conditioning by later sessions. Run convention: (a) is generative_process_redesign, the card used for agent-rewritten scaffolds (r08b Live-SWE-agent, r03b SICA, cal-dev Gödel Agent). (b) is adapt_via_conditioning, as for every retrieved-experience memory in this run. Both subs are null: C15/C23/C24 are generative-model tactics, and C03's canonical-schema training and category holdout are absent. son55's outside_taxonomy is a fair reading of the SDK as a whole, but the run identifies the self-improvement operations that are actually scored, not the surrounding engineering. Pattern matches never score.

claims.text: CCA reaches 59.0% Resolve@1 on SWE-Bench-Pro with GPT-5.2, exceeding prior research baselines and commercial results under identical repositories, backbone and tool access.
claims.setting: SWE-Bench-Pro public split (731 tasks), three-run mean, multiple backbones
claims.baseline_control: Author-run SWE-Agent and Live-SWE-Agent only for Claude 4 Sonnet / 4.5 Sonnet; Claude 4.5 Opus and GPT-5.2 baselines are proprietary-scaffold numbers copied from system cards
claims.selection_vs_test: meta-agent tuning set ('production-grade test set') not identified; overlap with evaluation unknown
claims.result_denominator: Claude4 Sonnet 42.7->45.5; Claude4.5 Sonnet SWE-Agent 43.6 / Live 45.8 -> CCA 52.7; Opus 52.0->54.3; GPT-5.2 56.0->59.0; no variance
claims.allowed_conclusion: In matched environments with Claude backbones, CCA scaffolding outperforms SWE-Agent/Live-SWE-Agent (author-run); comparison to proprietary results is unmatched and the 59.0 headline is not isolated to any retained component.

claims.text: Meta-agent-learned tool-use conventions are a major driver of CCA's performance.
claims.baseline_control: naive/simple SWE-Agent-like tool use (not a human-tuned alternative)
claims.selection_vs_test: same benchmark used to develop and evaluate; unspecified
claims.allowed_conclusion: The advanced tool stack beats a naive stack by 7 points on a 100-task subset; that this stack was produced by the meta-agent loop (vs. manual engineering) is not tested.

claims.text: Persistent notes give cross-session learning (fewer turns/tokens, higher resolve).
claims.setting: 151 instances that received notes, rerun on the same instances, Claude 4.5 Sonnet
claims.baseline_control: Run 1 without notes (no second no-notes run)
claims.selection_vs_test: notes written from and reused on the same tasks
claims.result_denominator: turns 64->61, tokens 104k->93k, Resolve 53.0->54.4; only instances with distilled notes
claims.allowed_conclusion: On tasks that produced notes, rerunning with those notes cost slightly less and resolved +1.4pt (single comparison); not shown to transfer to unseen tasks.

claims.text: Hierarchical memory + context compression improves long-context reasoning.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Prevents overflow; accuracy gain shown for one backbone on a selected subset only. Within-session, not a retained harness change.

G.reason: Opus sides with son55. The limitation is real but broad: flat histories, hand-tuned prompts/tool wiring, context overflow. Neighbours are named (SWE-Agent, OpenHands, Agentless, Live-SWE-Agent, Satori-SWE), but no baseline failure is measured. The residual over Live-SWE-Agent, which already self-edits prompts/tools/config, is not stated, and automated agent-design work (ADAS-type) is absent. sol's 3 credited a gap whose residue (sol:'remaining_gap') sol itself left open.

M.reason: Opus sides with son55. The mechanisms can be restated (Architect compression, asynchronous hindsight notes, a meta-agent that reads traces and patches prompts/extensions). But the meta-agent's candidate generation and acceptance criteria, and any prediction that separates it from manual tuning, are missing. Notes are written without outcome grounding. A concrete mechanism with a thin causal account is anchor 2.

X.reason: Opus sides with son55. For both retention paths, the condition that makes a change persist is absent, not merely unclear. The meta-agent applies patches and reruns 'until target metrics are met', with no per-edit accept/reject, rollback or version record. The run that produced CCA is not described (test set, iterations, what was accepted). Notes have no admission gate beyond a self-judged skip and no maintenance policy. The read path is only 'pass the note directory'. The interfaces themselves (memory tree, tools) are described, which keeps X above 0.

E.measurement.reason: Shared-error correction (both seats 3). The official test-based Resolve Rate is a credible metric. But the reported numbers fail the run's reporting-integrity check. Table 2's 48.6 and 51.6 are not attainable on the captioned 100-example subset (single run or 3-run mean), and §3.4.1 describes a different, outcome-filtered subset. Table 3's 49.2/203 and 44.1/86 are unattainable, and its buckets cover 639 of 731 tasks. Table 4's Run 2 54.4 % is not k/151 (or k/453). The commercial rows are system-card numbers under a caption claiming identical environments. Same cap as r09b EvoRoute/AgentDevel.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Same-backbone, same-environment SWE-Agent and Live-SWE-Agent comparisons, plus the advanced-vs-simple tool ablation (51.0 vs 44.0), give some attribution. There is no meta-agent-vs-manual or rival-optimizer control. The context-management subset is selected on both variants producing executable solutions. The notes contrast is Run 1 vs Run 2 on the same tasks, with a possible configuration difference (opus:O04).

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. SWE-Bench-Pro/Verified are external benchmarks, so not 0. But the meta-agent's 'production-grade test set' is not identified or separated from the evaluation, and the notes are generated on and re-evaluated on the same 151 tasks (Appendix F shows instance-specific fixes).

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked (A2 ladder). The main results are three-run means with stated sample sizes and no variance. The ablations (100/50/151 tasks) and the +1.4 notes gain have no uncertainty, and the denominator inconsistencies (opus:O01) leave the failure counts unclear.

E.cost.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. Only the notes run reports turns/tokens (system prompt excluded). Meta-agent iterations and cost, note-taking cost, and token parity with baselines are absent.

reason: Complete pinned v6 text incl. Appendices A–H read. In scope as a mixed A/B paper: the meta-agent's build-test-improve edits to non-weight prompts/tools and the persistent cross-session notes are the scored RSI parts. The SDK/AX-UX-DX engineering is context. All eight items resolved.

resolutions.reason: EVIDENCE rule 2: the notes are generated on and re-run on the same 151 tasks, so the selection set is the test set and evidence is at most 'task'. The tool ablation removes the meta-agent-derived stack in favour of a naive SWE-Agent-like stack. It does not compare the loop's retained change with the pre-loop state, and the loop's tuning set is unknown. No retained change is shown to cause later gains on independent tasks.

See rs_pattern.reason. The scored RSI operation (an agent rewriting a scaffold's hand-designed prompts/tools from traces) follows the run convention (Live-SWE-agent, SICA). son55's outside_taxonomy describes the SDK, not the scored loop.
Follows primary. adapt_via_conditioning is supporting for the notes path, sub null.
